author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Boston Logan International Airport is expected to add TSA PreCheck E-gates using facial-comparison technology, along with 3D scanners designed to inspect bags without requiring travelers to unpack them manually.

TSA Administrator David Cummins told CBS News Boston that PreCheck travelers would be able to keep a driver’s license and boarding pass in their pocket while moving through the gate. The bag scanners would create a three-dimensional view that lets screeners digitally inspect contents.

Travelers outside PreCheck are also expected to see walk-through body-scanning technology that does not require passengers to raise their hands. The report did not provide a firm installation date, so travelers should not assume the new process is available on a particular trip until Logan or TSA confirms it.

A separate program allowing some PreCheck members without tickets to accompany arriving or departing travelers is operating at 13 airports. Logan has not joined that program; an airport spokesperson said officials are monitoring it. That distinction matters because the planned screening equipment and visitor-access policy are separate changes.
dek: TSA says facial-comparison gates and 3D bag scanners are coming to Logan, while a separate visitor-access program remains under review.
headline: Logan Airport plans E-gates and scanners that digitally unpack bags
